Your post write updates only one feed in kv, so followers whose feeds should include the new post never receive it. That cannot keep the home feed promised in the statement, because a post must update every feed it belongs to, not just the author's.
points.quote: write POST:     client > lb > api > ids > kv then invalidate cache

Your seats table uses show as its primary key, so the database keeps only one seat per show and later seats overwrite earlier ones. The seat map for a show cannot list all its seats, and bookings for different seats in the same show clobber each other.
points.quote: table db.seats(show_id pk, seat_id, status, booking_id) index(seat_id)

Your primary key is created_at, but links are looked up and must stay unique by code. Links created at the same time can share that timestamp and overwrite each other, and this key does nothing to stop one code serving two urls.
points.quote: table db.links(created_at pk, code, url) index(code)

Your primary key is user_id, so only one job row can exist per user. A later send to the same user overwrites the earlier record, so an accepted send is lost from the database instead of every send being recorded.
